questions.h: Which condition is checked first, and is it true for 15?
questions.e: 15 is divisible by 3 and 5, so the first branch runs and the rest are skipped.
7 % 2 is 1, so the condition is false and the ternary gives "odd".

questions.h: Write the values of i until i > 0 fails.
questions.e: i takes the values 10, 7, 4 and 1, so the body runs 4 times.

questions.h: When does a do-while check its condition?
questions.e: A do-while runs its body once before checking. i becomes 6, then 6 < 5 is false, so it stops.

questions.h: Count the inner rounds for i = 1, 2, 3 and 4.
questions.e: The inner loop runs 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 times in total.

questions.h: Is there a break after any case?
questions.e: There is no break, so after case 2 runs, execution falls through into case 3 as well.

questions.q: Which loop always runs its body at least once?
questions.h: Which loop checks its condition after the body?
questions.e: do-while checks its condition after the body, so the body runs at least once.

questions.h: Each round takes n % 10 and attaches it to the right of r.
questions.e: Each round takes the last digit of n and attaches it to r, which reverses the number.

questions.q: To print 1, 3, 5, … up to N without an if, what should the loop's update be?
questions.h: Start at the first odd number and jump straight to the next odd one.
questions.e: Start at 1 and jump by 2: every value visited is odd, so no if is needed.

questions.h: Which of the three numbers is the largest?
questions.e: -2 is the largest of -5, -2 and -9. Starting below every value (or at the first one) keeps the answer correct for negatives.
